record.original_question: Suppose (p1,N, ..., pℓ,N) is a good sequence of ℓ-tuples of real polynomials, meaning every nontrivial linear combination of the sequences p1,N, ..., pℓ,N is good in the sense that its exponential sums against every nonzero frequency tend to zero. Must it follow that for every ergodic system (X, X, µ, T) and f1, ..., fℓ ∈ L∞(µ), the averages (1/N) Σ T^[p1,N(n)] f1 · ... · T^[pℓ,N(n)] fℓ converge in L2(µ) to ∫f1 dµ · ... · ∫fℓ dµ?

evidence.quote: Problem 10. Suppose that the sequence of ℓ-tuples of polynomials (p1,N , . . . , pℓ,N ) is good. Show that for every ergodic system (X, X , µ, T) and functions f1, . . . , fℓ ∈ L∞(µ) we have lim 1/N Σ T^[p1,N(n)]f1 · · · T^[pℓ,N(n)]fℓ = ∫ f1 dµ · · · ∫ fℓ dµ where convergence takes place in L2(µ).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\ell\ge 1$. For each $N\in\mathbb N$ let $p_{1,N},\dots,p_{\ell,N}\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be real polynomials. For a sequence $a\colon\mathbb N\to\mathbb R$ define its exponential sums by $E_N(a,t)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}e^{2\pi i\,t\,a(n)}$. Call a sequence $(a_N(n))_{N,n}$ (with $a_N$ depending on $N$ and $n$ ranging over $1,\dots,N$) "good" if for every $t\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$ one has $\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}e^{2\pi i t\,a_N(n)}\to 0$ as $N\to\infty$. Call the family of $\ell$-tuples $(p_{1,N},\dots,p_{\ell,N})_{N\in\mathbb N}$ good if every nontrivial integer (equivalently real) linear combination $c_1 p_{1,N}+\cdots+c_\ell p_{\ell,N}$, $(c_1,\dots,c_\ell)\ne 0$, gives a good sequence in the above sense.

Prove or disprove: whenever $(p_{1,N},\dots,p_{\ell,N})_{N\in\mathbb N}$ is good in this sense, then for every ergodic invertible measure-preserving system $(X,\mathcal X,\mu,T)$ and all $f_1,\dots,f_\ell\in L^\infty(\mu)$, the multiple ergodic averages
$$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} \big(T^{\lfloor p_{1,N}(n)\rfloor}f_1\big)\cdots\big(T^{\lfloor p_{\ell,N}(n)\rfloor}f_\ell\big)$$
converge in $L^2(\mu)$, as $N\to\infty$, to $\int f_1\,d\mu\,\cdots\int f_\ell\,d\mu$.
artifact.category_tag: multiple ergodic averages along variable polynomials
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in Frantzikinakis's list of open problems on multiple ergodic averages and is referenced in recent surveys (e.g., a 2026 survey on joint ergodicity) which note that the area remains full of open problems and direct readers to the maintained problem list for updates. No source located reports a full resolution of the variable-polynomial good-implies-joint-ergodicity question; partial results exist for fixed polynomials and specific Hardy-field families.
